How Kubernetes, helm and these images behave: A StatefulSet with updateStrategy RollingUpdate replaces its pods one at a time from the highest ordinal, deleting each old pod before it creates its replacement (there is no surge); with partition N, pods with an ordinal below N keep the old version; with OnDelete no pod is replaced until someone deletes it. A replacement pod mounts the same PVCs from volumeClaimTemplates. A pod's emptyDir volumes and its container filesystem are deleted together with the pod; only data on a PersistentVolume outlives it. When a PVC is deleted, its PersistentVolume and the data on it are deleted if the reclaimPolicy is Delete; with Retain the volume and its directory stay on the node (Released). Deleting a StatefulSet or scaling it down keeps the PVCs created from its volumeClaimTemplates, unless its persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy says Delete for that case (whenDeleted or whenScaled). A StatefulSet pod that is deleted is recreated with the same name and the same PVC name; if that PVC is gone, a new empty one is created. redis keeps its keys in memory. When the pod is deleted, redis gets SIGTERM and writes an RDB snapshot to its dir only if save points are configured (save not empty); with appendonly yes it has also been logging every write to its dir. A new redis process loads its keys from that dir. A Service sends connections only to ready pods whose labels match every key of its selector, on its targetPort (a number, or the name of a container port of those pods); with no such pod, or nothing listening there, connections fail.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
